audit.title: Supported Networks

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: The Streams Trade section does answer-first well ("available on the following networks:" + list). But the primary question — the full supported-networks matrix with addresses — is absent from extractable text.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean hierarchy, 1 H1, 0 level skips, sensible short sections. Undercut by the missing table, which is the natural chunk an engine would extract.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: 0 numerals, 0 hex identifiers, no chain IDs, no version strings. For a network reference page this is the highest-lift gap — addresses and chain IDs are exactly what agents query for.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 6 internal links to relevant concept pages (report schema, verification, Automation); no external/primary sources, and no block-explorer links because those live in the missing table.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: "Chainlink Data Streams provides data access directly via API or WebSocket for offchain use cases" is a solid liftable definition; Streams Trade is defined at first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: No JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, no og/twitter tags, head not captured. Weak across the board.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code blocks; largely not applicable for a networks list, so not penalized heavily.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Title matches "supported networks" queries; the Streams Trade list covers that sub-question. But "is <chain> supported for Data Streams," "verifier proxy address on <network>," and chain-ID lookups are unanswerable from the text.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent product naming (Data Streams, Streams Trade, StreamsLookup), unambiguous prose.

audit.summary: This is a network-support reference page for Chainlink Data Streams, whose entire purpose is to answer "which networks are supported and what are the verifier proxy addresses." The catastrophic problem: the page's own prose promises "The table below lists all networks supported by Data Streams... each with verifier proxy contracts," but the measured facts confirm **0 tables and 0 hex identifiers in the served content** — the core table is injected by the `<DataStreams section="dsNotes" />` component and never rendered into extractable HTML/markdown. A generative engine retrieving this page gets a promise with no payload. The honest verdict: prose quality is fine, but the single most valuable asset on the page is invisible to retrieval, which caps fidelity regardless of how well the rest reads.

recommendations.title: Render the supported-networks table as static text
recommendations.where: Body paragraph "The table below lists all networks supported by Data Streams…" (`<DataStreams section="dsNotes" />` component)
recommendations.issue: "The table below lists all networks…" — but 0 tables and 0 hex identifiers are in the served content.
recommendations.change: Ensure the component server-renders (or provide a static fallback) a real Markdown/HTML table with columns: Network, Chain ID, Verifier Proxy Address, Explorer link. This is the page's core payload and must exist in the raw HTML.
recommendations.why: An engine cannot cite or synthesize content that isn't in the retrieved text; this converts the page from a promise into an answer and injects the numerals/addresses currently scoring 2/10.

recommendations.title: Add per-network specifics (chain IDs, address strings)
recommendations.where: The same networks table and the Streams Trade bullet list.
recommendations.issue: Streams Trade list is name-only: "Arbitrum, Avalanche, Base, BNB Chain…" with no chain IDs.
recommendations.change: Append chain IDs to each entry (e.g., "Arbitrum (42161)", "Base (8453)") and include mainnet/testnet distinctions.
recommendations.why: Quantitative identifiers are among the highest-lift signals and match how agents query ("verifier proxy on chain 42161").

recommendations.title: Add symptom/query-phrased anchors
recommendations.issue: No headings phrased as the questions users ask.
recommendations.change: Add sections like "Which networks does Chainlink Data Streams support?" and "What is the verifier proxy address for <network>?" answered in the first sentence.
recommendations.why: Question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` schema and canonical URL
recommendations.issue: JSON-LD: 0 blocks; canonical MISSING; no dateModified.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, and a self-referential canonical URL; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise agent trust (E-E-A-T) and parse reliability. (Note: head wasn't captured — CLI should pass raw `<head>` to confirm absence.)

recommendations.title: Strengthen the lead definition as a standalone chunk
recommendations.issue: The definition is good but the following sentence depends on the unrendered table for meaning.
recommendations.change: Make the first sentence fully self-contained (e.g., "Chainlink Data Streams is supported on N networks, each with a deployed verifier proxy contract for onchain report verification.") with the count stated.
recommendations.why: A crisp, number-bearing opening survives skimming and parametric fallback.

antiPatterns: **Unresolved cross-reference to missing content:** "The table below lists all networks…" points to a table that does not exist in the served output — a broken promise for both readers and engines.
**Undated content:** No dateModified/datePublished; freshness cannot be signaled on a page whose accuracy (address deployments) is time-sensitive.
offPageNotes: The `llms.txt` reference is present and good; verify it indexes this page with the network matrix.

Component-rendered content (`<DataStreams>`) is a site-level rendering-pipeline issue — the fix (server-side rendering / static fallback) is architectural, not editorial, but it dominates this page's GEO ceiling.
Head metadata could not be verified from the provided content; pass raw `<head>` in the CLI for a complete metadata read.
